_meta.note: Hand-authored Chinese-speaking East Asia catalog: Hong Kong, Taipei, Kaohsiung, Shanghai, Beijing, Guangzhou and Singapore. Shaped like Qloo Insights entities plus a `_syn` block used for scoring and stripped before serving. Entity ids are fake. Not Qloo data.

properties.short_description: 'The Moon Represents My Heart', 'Sweet as Honey', 'Tsugunai', 'Toki no Nagare ni Mi o Makase': the voice of the whole Chinese-speaking world, and of Japan too.
'Not Going Home Today' (今天不回家, 1969): the Taiwanese singer whose sad songs were banned and sung everywhere.
The singer in the hat: 'Applause' (掌聲響起), 'I Am a Cloud'; Taiwan's sweetheart from 1972.
'Forgotten Time' (被遺忘的時光), 'Your Eyes': the low voice from the 1979 campus-folk contest.
'Past Love Can Only Be Remembered' (往事只能回味, 1970), the song of every karaoke since.
The king of Taiwanese Hokkien song: 'Mother, Please Take Care' (媽媽請你也保重), 'Lover in a Yellow Shirt'.
'Old Love at Tamsui Dusk' (淡水暮色), 'Old Love in the Rain': Hokkien songs with a trumpet voice.
'The Olive Tree' (橄欖樹, 1979): the campus-folk voice of Sanmao's lyrics.
The composer of 'One Plum Blossom' and 'Moonlight on the Lake Field'; two thousand songs for Taiwan's screen.
The Golden Voice of Shanghai: 'Shanghai Nights' (夜上海), 'When Will You Return?' (何日君再來), 'The Wandering Songstress'.
The husky contralto of 'Waiting for You to Return' (等著你回來) and 'If There Were No You'.
'Evening Primrose' (夜來香), 'Suzhou Nocturne': the Shanghai star who was really Yoshiko Yamaguchi.
'Rose, Rose, I Love You' (玫瑰玫瑰我愛你): from Shanghai's Pathé to Hong Kong's EMI, the silver voice.
'I Want Your Love', 'Carmen' and 'Mambo Girl': Hong Kong's singing, dancing star of the 1950s.
The voice behind the Shaw Brothers' huangmei films, 'The Love Eterne' and all.
'Ding Dong Song', 'Bengawan Solo' in Mandarin and English: the Shanghai-born songbird of Hong Kong's sixties.
'Eiffel Tower Above the Clouds', 'Games Gamblers Play' (鬼馬雙星), 'The Private Eyes': the God of Song who made Cantopop in 1974.
The Godfather of Cantopop: 'Below the Lion Rock' (獅子山下, 1979), 'The Bund', the TVB theme songs.
'Every Step' (每一步), 'Smile on the Road': the velvet contralto in the sequined gown, from Shanghai to Hong Kong.
'The Bund' (上海灘, 1980), the TVB theme song that the whole of Asia can sing.
'The Book and the Sword', 'Chor Lau-heung': the TVB swordsman who sang his own themes.
'The Yong Zheng Dynasty' theme, 'Wan Sui Ye': the Queen of TVB on stage and screen from 1971.
'Iron Blood, Loyal Heart' (鐵血丹心, 1983) with Roman Tam; the voice of The Legend of the Condor Heroes.
'Give Me a Kiss' (給我一個吻): the Shanghai girl who became the Queen of Mandarin pop in 1950s Hong Kong and Singapore.
'Love in Early Spring', 'Bengawan Solo': Singapore's Malayan Songstress of the 1950s and 60s.
'My Motherland' (我的祖国, 1956), 'The White-Haired Girl': the folk voice of the new China.
'Nostalgia' (乡恋, 1979), the first love song on Chinese television after the Cultural Revolution.
'On the Hopeful Fields' (在希望的田野上), 'Peony Song': the tenor of the early 1980s.
The soprano of 'The White-Haired Girl' ballet and the first Chinese pop recordings of the late 1970s.

properties.description: Li Han-hsiang's huangmei opera of Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai; Ivy Ling Po, and Taipei watching it a hundred times.
King Hu's Golden Swallow in the inn; the wuxia film reborn.
King Hu's inn in the desert, the eunuch's assassins and the swordsmen; Taiwan's record-breaker.
King Hu's bamboo forest fight and the Cannes prize of 1975.
Chang Cheh and Jimmy Wang Yu; the first Hong Kong film to make a million at the box office.
Bruce Lee at the ice factory; the film that started everything.
Bruce Lee kicks the sign at the Shanghai park gate; Chen Zhen and the Jingwu school.
The island tournament and the hall of mirrors; Bruce Lee's last completed film.
Chor Yuen's crowded tenement comedy that outgrossed Bruce Lee and brought Cantonese back to the screen.
The Hui brothers' first comedy, Michael and Sam, and the title song that made Cantopop.
Michael Hui's detective agency, Sam Hui's theme song, the kung-fu with sausages.
Grace Chang dancing the mambo in the Hong Kong musical that made her a star.
Grace Chang's Carmen in a Wan Chai nightclub.
Li Han-hsiang's emperor in disguise and the village girl; the Shaw Brothers' first huangmei hit.
Taiwan's 'healthy realism' begins on the Chiayi coast; the first colour film made by Taiwanese hands.
Lee Hsing's duck farmer and his daughter, the Taiwan countryside in colour.
The first Chiung Yao film: Wan-chun and her three cousins.
Brigitte Lin's first film, the schoolgirl and her teacher, from Chiung Yao's novel.

properties.description: Lee Hsing's woodcarver's family in Sanyi; Teresa Teng's title song.
Pai Ching-jui's returnees from America find their Taipei changed.
Xie Jin's Hainan women's company; the film and then the ballet.
The Bai girls of Dali and the Butterfly Spring; a love story in colour from the Great Leap years.
The Guangxi folk singer who outsings the landlord's scholars; the Li River in colour.
Xie Tieli's teacher in the river town, banned the year after; Sun Daolin and Xie Fang.
Xie Jin's two Shaoxing opera singers from the countryside to Shanghai.
The Hebei villagers' tunnels against the Japanese; shown to every child for decades.
The boy Pan Dongzi and his red star; the song of the 1970s classroom.
The Korean War film with 'Hymn of Heroes'; Wang Cheng at the hilltop.

entities.name: Big Li, Little Li and Old Li

properties.description: Xie Jin's Shanghai meat-factory comedy about getting fit.
Zhou Xuan sings 'The Wandering Songstress' at the teahouse window; old Shanghai's classic.
Fei Mu's ruined wall, a wife and the doctor who was her first love.
TVB's live variety show, every weeknight from the first day of the station, for 27 years.
Michael and Sam Hui's sketches and songs on TVB, where the brothers' comedy began.
RTHK's dramas of ordinary Hong Kong lives, and the Roman Tam theme that became the city's anthem.

entities.name: The Legend of the Book and the Sword

properties.description: TVB's first Jin Yong serial, Adam Cheng as Chen Jialuo.
TVB's first long-form drama, the hotel dynasty of 128 episodes.

entities.name: A House Is Not a Home

properties.description: Liza Wang's Lok Lam-sum and the family fortune; TVB's 110-episode saga.
Chow Yun-fat as Hui Man-keung in 1920s Shanghai, and Frances Yip's theme that never left.

entities.name: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly

properties.description: TVB's Chow Yun-fat as the mainland cousin Ah Chian; the catchphrases of a year.
RTV's long family saga, Patrick Tse and the tears that gave the show its name.
TTV's song show from the first year of Taiwanese television, the stage of Mandarin pop for fifteen years.
CTS's Yi Feng as the black-faced judge; 350 episodes of the Song dynasty court.
Huang Chun-hsiung's glove-puppet Shi Yan-wen on CTV, the show that stopped Taiwan at noon.
Taiwan's wartime drama with Liu Chia-chang's song.
CCTV's seven o'clock news, the same opening music every night since 1978.
CCTV's Monkey King, Liu Xiao Ling Tong, rerun every summer holiday since.
CCTV's thirty-six episodes of the Jia family, the Daiyu that a generation remembers.
SBC's drama of Singapore's early Chinese immigrants, the Teochew family and the river.
Dim sum from the trolleys and shared tables on Wellington Street, since 1926.
The art-deco tea house of 1933 on Stanley Street, ceiling fans and brass spittoons.
Roast goose on Wellington Street since 1942, from a dai pai dong to the gold-fronted restaurant.
Swiss chicken wings and soufflé at the soy-sauce Western restaurant, in Hong Kong since 1938.
The birthplace of silk-stocking milk tea, the Gage Street stall of 1952.
The Yau Ma Tei cha chaan teng of 1950, the booths, the tiles and the baked pork chop rice.

properties.description: Scrambled eggs, toast and steamed milk pudding in fifteen minutes flat, Jordan since 1970.
Wonton noodles in the small bowl, the Mak family's recipe from Guangzhou, in Hong Kong since 1968.
The egg tarts of Lyndhurst Terrace since 1954, Chris Patten's favourite.
The Western grill of 1928, the colonial dining room of Central.
Roast pigeon in the Sha Tin garden since 1951, Bruce Lee's favourite.
properties.address: 22 Ha Wo Che, Sha Tin, New Territories

properties.description: Xiaolongbao from the Xinyi Road oil shop that became a restaurant in 1972.
Soy milk and shaobing at dawn in the Huashan Market since 1958, the queue down the stairs.
Oyster vermicelli eaten standing in Ximending since 1975.
Braised beef noodle soup in the Yongkang Street original since 1963.

properties.description: The Russian café of 1949 on Wuchang Street where the writers of Taipei sat, Chiang Ching-kuo's wife's cakes.
Taipei's first Western restaurant, 1934, the date spot of Dadaocheng for three generations.
The Datong night market of 1954, oyster omelettes and taro balls.
Seventy flavours from pork floss to sesame oil chicken, Wuchang Street since 1947.
Kaohsiung's night market of 1950, papaya milk and seafood on Liuhe Road.
Shanghai's old restaurant of 1875 by Yu Garden: eight-treasure duck and red-braised pork.
Xiaolongbao by the zigzag bridge at Yu Garden since 1900, the longest queue in the city.
Mooncakes and Cantonese dishes on Fuzhou Road since 1851.
Borscht and pork chops at the oldest Western restaurant in Shanghai, since 1897.
The French restaurant of 1935 on Huaihai Road, baked clams and the old waiters.
Qingtuan and rice cakes from the Nanjing Road sweet shop of 1875.
Peking duck roasted over fruitwood since 1864, the Qianmen original.
Mutton hot pot in the copper pot, Wangfujing since 1903.
'Lao Mo', the Soviet-built restaurant of 1954 at the Exhibition Center, borscht and the chandeliers.
Douzhi, wandouhuang and the old Beijing snacks, Huguosi Street since 1956.
Closed-oven roast duck, the older style, since 1416.
The 1939 Cantonese restaurant of Wenchang Road, morning tea and the courtyard.
Dim sum in the garden pavilions by the Liwan lake since 1947.
The Cantonese tea house of 1880 on Dishifu Road.
The Singapore Sling and peanut shells on the floor, the hotel of 1887.
The open-air satay stalls on Beach Road, from the 1940s until 1995.
Hainanese chicken rice on Purvis Street since 1940, the oldest in town.
The oldest Chinese restaurant in Singapore, 1929.
The Peak Tram since 1888 and the harbour lights from the top.
The green-and-white ferries across the harbour since 1888, ten minutes for a few cents.
properties.address: Star Ferry Pier, Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon

properties.description: The rides, the ice rink and the Cantonese opera, from 1949 until 1997.
The Haw Par mansion's garden of 1935 with its painted hell and pagoda; demolished in 2004.
The beach of the south side, the old Repulse Bay Hotel and the Tin Hau statues.
The night market of Yau Ma Tei, fortune tellers and Cantonese opera singers.
properties.address: Temple Street, Yau Ma Tei, Kowloon

properties.description: The cable car over the sea since 1977, the dolphins and the rides.
The approach over the rooftops of Kowloon City, 1925 to 1998.
The Causeway Bay theatre of 1927, Cantonese opera and the Miss Hong Kong pageant; demolished in 1991.
properties.address: Percival Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong

properties.description: The Taoist temple of 1921 where every wish is answered, the fortune sticks on New Year's Eve.
properties.address: 2 Chuk Yuen Village, Wong Tai Sin, Kowloon

properties.description: Wednesday nights at the races since 1845, the floodlights and the city around the track.
The Japanese department store of 1960 in Causeway Bay, the first of its kind in Hong Kong; closed in 1998.
properties.address: Paterson Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong

properties.description: The 1962 concert hall and library on the Edinburgh Place waterfront.
The 1915 tower of the old Kowloon railway station, all that is left of it on the waterfront.
The cinema district of Taipei, the Red House of 1908 and the pedestrian streets.
The Wanhua temple of 1738, incense and the chanting at dusk.
The park of 1908 by the Presidential Office, the radio station and the pavilions; 228 Peace Park since 1996.
The jade cabbage and the meat-shaped stone, the imperial collection in Shilin since 1965.
The red palace hotel of 1952 on the hill above the Keelung River.
properties.address: 1 Zhongshan North Road Section 4, Zhongshan, Taipei

properties.description: The Taipei zoo of 1914 beside the Grand Hotel, Lin Wang the elephant; moved to Muzha in 1986.
The old merchants' street of Dadaocheng, dried goods and the Lunar New Year market.
The 1936 hall where the Japanese surrender was received; concerts and films after.
The old port at the river mouth, Fisherman's Wharf and the sunset of the song.
The hot-spring valley of Japanese-era bathhouses at the end of the line.
The white hall and the blue roof of 1980, the square where the city gathers.
The river through Kaohsiung, the evening walk and the lantern festival.
The ferry across the harbour, the seafood street and the lighthouse.
The Dragon and Tiger Pagodas of 1976 and the temples around the lake at Zuoying.
The waterfront of banks and the Peace Hotel, the Huangpu and the evening crowds.
The shopping street from the Bund to People's Square, the No. 1 Department Store of 1936.
The Ming garden, the zigzag bridge and the Huxinting teahouse in the old town.
The amusement palace of 1917 with its tower, the funhouse mirrors and the opera stages.
The green pyramid roof of 1929 on the Bund, the old jazz band in the bar.
The art-deco cinema of 1928 on People's Square, the best screen in old Shanghai.
The old racecourse of Shanghai, a park since 1952, the marriage market on weekends.
The golden temple in the middle of the shopping district, on the site since 1216.
The Xijiao Park zoo of 1954, the giant pandas and the lawns.
The French park of 1909, the rose garden and the dancers in the morning.
The great square, the flag at sunrise and the Gate of Heavenly Peace.
The Palace Museum, nine thousand rooms of the Ming and Qing emperors.
The blue-tiled Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests and the park full of tai chi and card games.
Kunming Lake, the Long Corridor and the marble boat; skating in winter, boats in summer.
The White Dagoba on the island, the rowing boats and the song every child learned.
The shopping street of the capital, the Beijing Department Store of 1955 and the snack street.
The oldest zoo in China, 1906, the pandas in the west of the city.
The stadium of 1959 in Chaoyang, the National Games and the football.
The three lakes north of Beihai, the hutongs around them and the winter ice.
The old concession island of banyan trees and colonial mansions on the Pearl River.
The Five Rams statue of 1960 and the Zhenhai Tower on the hill.
The China Import and Export Fair, twice a year since 1957.
The Tiger Balm Gardens of 1937, the Ten Courts of Hell and the painted statues.
Rides, cabarets and the Sky Theatre on Kim Seng Road, from 1929 until 1978.
The grand cinema of 1930 at Stamford Road, Hollywood for Singapore.
Queen Elizabeth Walk along the waterfront, the satay smell and the sea breeze.
The crescent of five diamonds at the foot of Fort Canning, 1963 to 1984.
The lake in the mountains, the honeymoon of a generation and the boat to Lalu Island.
The forest railway, the sunrise over the sea of clouds and the cherry blossoms.
The marble gorge and the Central Cross-Island Highway of 1960.
The beaches at the southern tip, the lighthouse and the Kenting street at night.
The old capital: Chihkan Tower, Anping Fort and the danzai noodles.
The ferry from Hong Kong, the ruins of St Paul's, Portuguese egg tarts and the casinos.
The dumbbell island, the ferry, the bun festival and the seafood on the praya.
Po Lin Monastery, the Big Buddha of 1993 and the beaches of Cheung Sha.
West Lake, the Broken Bridge and Longjing tea; heaven above, Suzhou and Hangzhou below.
The classical gardens, the canals and the silk, an hour from Shanghai.
The Yellow Mountains, the pines on the granite and the sea of clouds.
The karst hills along the Li River, the scenery on the twenty-yuan note.
The seaside resort of the capital, the beach and the leaders' summer villas.
The sacred mountain, the sunrise from the Jade Emperor Peak after the night climb.
The German villas, the beaches and the beer.
The mountain resort of villas and mist, the 1980 film that every couple went to see.
The restored wall of 1957, the first section everyone climbs.
The ferry, the hawker food and the hill railway; Singapore's holiday up the coast.
Tea plantations, strawberries and the cool air of the hill station.
